claims.text: Substituting approximately 10 at.% Cr with Mn reduces atomic size mismatch in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys.
Reduced atomic size mismatch decreases local lattice distortion.
Reduced local lattice distortion decreases the magnitude of short-range ordering.
Suppression of short-range ordering stabilizes a predominantly disordered FCC phase.
A stable disordered FCC phase underpins a beneficial balance of high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness.
Atomic size mismatch produces lattice strain that promotes short-range-order formation.
The controlled comparison uses an undoped baseline and an alloy in which approximately 10 at.% Cr is replaced by Mn.
Both principal comparison samples are homogenized at 1200 °C for 1 hour, annealed at 800 °C for 24 hours, and subjected to controlled cooling.
Local lattice distortion and short-range-order parameters can be quantified using X-ray or neutron pair-distribution-function analysis.
Relative to the baseline, the Mn-modified alloy will have significantly lower short-range-order parameters.
Relative to the baseline, the Mn-modified alloy will retain a larger fraction of disordered FCC phase.
Relative to the baseline, the Mn-modified alloy will exhibit enhanced cryogenic toughness and radiation tolerance.
The predicted improvements in cryogenic toughness and radiation tolerance will occur without sacrificing high-temperature strength or environmental resistance.
Electronic-structure changes caused by Mn substitution could confound attribution of the response to lattice distortion.
The proposed mechanism is limited to the specified heat treatment and to compositions in which electronic effects do not overwhelm lattice-distortion effects.

contradictions.description: The control dopant is introduced to separate lattice-size effects from electronic effects, and similar behavior from a similarly sized but electronically benign dopant would ordinarily support a lattice-distortion mechanism. The falsification rule instead states that similar effects in the control indicate that the response is not solely due to reduced lattice strain, reversing the stated interpretation of the control.
